text_blocks.snippet: Type 2 diabetes is diagnosed using specific blood tests evaluated by a healthcare provider.
snippet_highlighted_words: using specific blood tests evaluated by a healthcare provider

list.snippet: A1C Test: Measures your average blood sugar level over the past 2 to 3 months.
Diabetes threshold: 6.5% or higher on two separate tests.
Fasting Plasma Glucose (FPG) Test: Measures your blood sugar after you do not eat or drink anything except water for at least 8 hours.
Diabetes threshold: 126 mg/dL or higher on two separate tests.
Oral Glucose Tolerance Test (OGTT): Measures your blood sugar 2 hours after you drink a special sugary liquid.
Diabetes threshold: 200 mg/dL or higher after 2 hours.
Random Plasma Glucose Test: Measures your blood sugar at any time of day.
Diabetes threshold: 200 mg/dL or higher when you also have classic symptoms of diabetes (such as extreme thirst, frequent urination, or unexplained weight loss).

text_blocks.snippet: In most cases without severe symptoms, doctors will repeat the diagnostic test on a second day to confirm the result. You can read more detailed guidelines from the American Diabetes Association or review overview information on MedlinePlus.
